content: The Department of Global HIV, Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infection Programmes is collaborating with WHO Press to maximize the visibility of WHO products at major conferences, such as the International AIDS Society conferences and the Conferences for Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections. Once approved by the Guidelines Review Committee, the updated guidelines will be published on the WHO HIV website. These guidelines will incorporate recommendations developed for this update, as well as other relevant guidance released since 2016, and will be integrated into the updated consolidated HIV guidelines scheduled for release in July 2021. The publication will initially be available in English, with translations into other official languages coordinated with regional and country offices. The recommendations and supporting information will also be accessible through the WHO HIV Tx App, a free mobile application available globally for download on major app stores. Additional dissemination materials, such as printed documents, PDFs, and social media links, will be provided to communicate key messages of WHO recommendations. Key annexes containing systematic reviews and other supporting information will be uploaded to the WHO website. Derivative products, including slide sets, question-and-answer documents, and webinars, will be developed to assist countries in adapting and implementing the guidelines in their specific contexts. The Department of Global HIV, Viral Hepatitis, and Sexually Transmitted Infection Programmes monitors the adoption of HIV-related recommendations through mechanisms such as the Global AIDS Monitoring framework, in-country surveys, and population-based HIV impact assessments. These tools provide indirect evidence of the impact of WHO recommendations. The department will work with WHO regional and country offices to monitor the uptake and implementation of the guidelines. Potential barriers include delays in dissemination due to translation time and limited resources in some countries to update existing policies. The guidelines will be updated using a modular process, with ongoing scoping reviews conducted to anticipate future guidance needs. When necessary, rapid guidance and technical or operational updates will complement the guideline updates. The WHO 2013 consolidated guidelines for antiretroviral therapy, which combined recommendations across the continuum of HIV care for the first time, were updated in 2016. Since then, emerging evidence from clinical and operational studies has necessitated further updates to normative guidance. Supplementary guidelines have been published using a modular approach to address new evidence. The updated consolidated guidelines planned for 2021 will include revised recommendations on HIV prevention, infant diagnosis, antiretroviral initiation, and monitoring. They will also feature updated service delivery recommendations, which are being developed through a separate guideline process. The guideline development process involves consultations and scoping reviews conducted by WHO staff across all areas of HIV work. Technical scoping meetings were held to formulate population, intervention, comparison, and outcome (PICO) questions relevant to the guidelines, addressing research gaps identified in previous meetings. The guideline development process followed the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) methodology to assess the certainty of evidence and determine the strength of recommendations. Systematic reviews were conducted to address PICO questions, complemented by supporting information on feasibility, acceptability, costs, cost-effectiveness, and disease modeling. The evidence was synthesized and presented in GRADE evidence profile tables, which included relative and absolute effect estimates and certainty ratings. The Guideline Development Group met virtually from September 28 to October 2, 2020, due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The group reached consensus on all recommendations without requiring a vote. Systematic reviews and evidence-to-decision-making tables were shared in advance and discussed during the meetings. The group considered factors such as the certainty of evidence, benefits and risks, values and preferences, cost implications, equity, acceptability, and feasibility when formulating recommendations. All external contributors to the guidelines, including members of the Guideline Development Group and the External Review Group, completed WHO declarations of interest forms. These were reviewed to identify potential conflicts of interest, and management plans were developed as needed. The draft guidelines were circulated for peer review to members of both groups in November 2020.
